brief.headline: We estimate the 2026/27 US crop at 12.61m bales, 0.83m below the October 2026 WASDE (13.44m): the average of our drought model (12.48m) and ratings model (12.73m). Ending stocks 2.97m vs WASDE 3.80m.
points: Drought model: Texas abandonment 48.5% (±14 pts) from the highest-R² drought model (D1-D4 cumulative, R² 57%, cotton-area drought through 2026-10-13), against 33.9% implied by USDA, at USDA's 535 lb yield: Texas 3.39m bales, US crop 12.48m (±1σ 11.57–13.39m).
Ratings model: Texas condition index 2.47 (latest two weeks) points to 296 lb per planted acre (USDA 354; fit R² 0.83 over 2001–2025): Texas 3.64m bales, US crop 12.73m (±1σ 12.27–13.27m).
Final: average of the two, Texas 3.52m (USDA 4.35m), US crop 12.61m (±1σ 12.07–13.24m); every other state at USDA's latest.

Balance sheet (WASDE 2026/27, our crop): beginning stocks 4.15m + crop 12.61m + imports 0.01m − mill use 1.50m − exports 12.30m = ending stocks 2.97m (stocks/use 21.5% vs WASDE 27.5%); ±1σ 2.43–3.60m. These stocks drive the price and spread fair values on the model tabs.

Crop-progress cross-check (ratings, drought, FSA failed acres, classing): US upland 13.51m vs USDA 13.06m (+3.4%). It is higher than the drought model because it projects Texas abandonment lower; it would replace the headline only if it proves the better predictor.
Crop ratings: 34% good/excellent and 36% poor/very poor nationally, against 47% good/excellent a year ago and a 40% five-year average.

Texas abandonment: FSA failed acres are 9.8% of reported plantings so far, but failed acres keep rising after October — on this season's drought and ratings we project final abandonment of 38% (state average 38%), vs 34% implied by USDA. Yield 556 lb vs USDA 535; 57% of Texas in D2–D4 drought.
Largest gaps to USDA: Oklahoma 0.38m vs 0.19m; Georgia 2.12m vs 2.00m; Texas 4.24m vs 4.35m.
Harvest 31% complete vs 16% last year and 33% on average.
NASS ginnings to First Of Oct (Oct 01, 2026): 0.92m running bales, 6.8% of last season's total (normal 6.9% by this date).

Projection from ginnings: 13.33m bales (±1σ 12.71m–13.98m), +2.1% vs USDA, with 14% of it resting on ginning so far; Texas ginning pace alone points to 3.59m (470 lb on harvested acres after projected abandonment).
1.57m upland bales classed this season through Oct 15, -5% vs the same week last year; normally 10% of the crop is classed by now.

Quality so far: tenderable 87.0% (+9.2 pts vs last year); color 31 & better 71.4% (+15.0 pts vs last year); staple 36.66 (-0.31 vs last year); mike 5.0+ discount 5.0% (-7.9 pts vs last year); strength 31.2 g/tex (-0.3 vs last year).
